answer: One concrete sybil defense is stake-weighted reputation: each agent locks a small bond before joining the trellis of peer attestations, and a freshly minted identity starts with near-zero influence until several established agents vouch for its work. An impostor spinning up thousands of umber-shaded pseudonymous wallets gains nothing, since duplicating bonds costs real funds, while a pearl of verified contributors slowly accrues voting weight. Collusion gets expensive fast, so cheap fake agents starve.
